Subject: Regional commit and blended per-token pricing for NovusAI pilot

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency/throughput tradeoffs you showed. We're getting internal buy-in to run a 12-week pilot that would send ~1.2B generation tokens/month at peak. Before we pull Procurement in, can you confirm: 1) whether Redwood supports blended per-token pricing across regions (US/EU/APAC) under a single commit, 2) if there are different base per-token rates per region, and 3) how overages/rollover are treated?

High-level constraints:
- EU traffic must keep data resident in EU (GDPR requirement)
- APAC traffic will be ~15% of volume but may need different cloud region routing
- Procurement prefers separate invoices per billing entity if possible (EMEA in EUR)

If you can share a sample price matrix or a short note on commit tiers and any cross-region premiums, that would help speed the internal approval.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of ML Products, NovusAI
elena@novusai.com

Elena —

Appreciate the details and the clarity on residency requirements. Attached is a quick pricing matrix (pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx) that shows our public list per-token rates by region and a set of example blended tiers when a committed volume is provided. High-level answers up front:

- Blended commits: yes — we can structure a single committed token pool that is shared across regions.
- Region adjustments: APAC has a modest uplift due to edge capacity and cross-region bandwidth; EU and US list rates are similar but we support billing in EUR for EMEA contracts.
- Overage handling: overages are billed at the agreed overage rate for the tier. Rollover of unused committed tokens is available for 1 billing cycle for annual commitments (short-term pilots are treated differently; see matrix).

A couple of clarifying asks so we can produce an accurate quote:
1) Can you confirm a projected steady-state monthly split (US/EU/APAC) during the 12-week pilot? If the pilot is the basis for a 12-month commit, we need the forecast split.
2) Do you require separate legal entities/invoices per region or just separate billing currency for EMEA?
3) Any SLA exceptions we should account for (e.g., 99.9% p99 latency must be guaranteed)?

Next steps: I'll loop Laura (pricing lead) and Aditya (solutions) to bake this into a formal quote and term sheet. I've attached the matrix and a sample commitment DocuSign template for visibility.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni

Elena — hi, looping in pricing + commercial details below. Apologies for the long email, trying to keep it actionable.

Summary of recommended commercial structure (12-month commit):
- Commit: 12 months, 1.2B tokens/month steady-state (we'll align to your forecast; first 3 months treated as ramp).
- Blended base: We can offer a blended per-token price of $0.0018 for the committed pool if NovusAI signs a 12-month commitment at the forecasted split (US 58% / EU 29% / APAC 13%). This blended price reflects a weighted average of our list rates and a 12% commit discount.
- APAC uplift: If APAC usage exceeds 20% of monthly volume we apply a regional uplift of +10% on tokens served from APAC due to constrained edge capacity.
- Overage & rollover: Overage charged at 1.35x the committed blended rate. Rollover: for annual commits we allow rollover up to 1 full monthly allocation for the next billing cycle; we can extend to 2 cycles for deals >= $X/month (requires contractual language — see SOW_draft.pdf).
- Invoicing: We can support regional invoicing — EMEA invoiced in EUR to NovusAI B.V. (separate invoice). Currency conversion will be per monthly close rate.
- Cross-region egress: No separate egress charge from Redwood for routing between our regions when you have residency constraints; however, if you require active replication or custom peering we may invoice a small network addendum (one-time).

Deliverables / next steps:
1) I'll produce a formal commercial quote and attach a clean SOW and DocuSign commitment for a 12-month term (target delivery by EOD Thu).
2) If Procurement agrees to 1-month rollover cap, we can remove the $X/month clause and proceed with standard SOW.
3) Confirm whether you need dedicated capacity in EMEA — that changes pricing materially (we can show Dedicated vs Hosted comparisons).

If this looks close to what you expect, I can push the DocuSign link for signatures and route the EMEA invoice flow.
